scenes.image: Victoria standing at the head of a long Thanksgiving table, glass raised, looking down the table with a cold smile.
lines: [sharp, cutting through the chatter] Emma. Stand up.
sfx: Thanksgiving dinner chatter, silverware, soft jazz piano

scenes.image: Emma seated at the table, fork frozen halfway, looking up in confusion.
lines: [slowly, enjoying it] You heard me. Stand. Up.

scenes.image: Close-up of Victoria tapping a crystal glass with a silver spoon, guests turning to look.
lines: [loud, theatrical] For four years, I have tolerated a woman who married my son for his money.
sfx: A spoon tapping a crystal glass, then the room going silent

scenes.image: Victoria pointing down the table at Emma, guests staring.
lines: [cold] You have ten minutes to collect your things and get out of my house.

scenes.image: Emma standing, sliding her wedding ring off, setting it beside her untouched plate.
lines: [steady, barely above a whisper] Before I go, Victoria... are you absolutely certain this house belongs to you?
scenes.motion: she slowly slides the ring off her finger and sets it down beside the plate

scenes.image: Victoria laughing in disbelief, one hand on her pearls.
lines: [calm, cold] Then I hope you have the paperwork.
sfx: Music cuts out abruptly, then a deep cinematic boom

scenes.image: Ryan at the table, pale, avoiding everyone's eyes, his hand trembling around his glass.
lines: [low] Behind her, Victoria laughed. But Ryan didn't. [pause] Because he knew something his mother didn't. And Emma was about to find out.

scenes.image: Three weeks earlier: Ryan rushing into the kitchen holding a thick stack of papers and a pen; Emma pouring coffee.
lines: [hurried, distracted] Babe, I need you to sign something.
[dry, half smiling] Good morning to you too.

scenes.image: Ryan dropping a thick stack of documents on the counter and clicking a pen.
lines: [sighs] Sorry. I'm running late. Just business documents.
sfx: Heavy stack of papers dropped on a counter

scenes.image: Emma reading the documents closely, frowning, finger stopping on a line.
lines: [slowly] Why does it say three million dollars?

scenes.image: Emma looking up at Ryan skeptically; Ryan checking his watch.
lines: Then why does it need my signature?
[flat] That's not how business loans work, Ryan.

scenes.image: Ryan leaning on the counter, jaw tight, irritated.
lines: [sharp] You always have to question everything.
I worked in finance before I joined your company. I know what a personal guarantee looks like.
[cold] Are you calling me a liar?

scenes.image: Emma calmly setting down her coffee, holding his gaze.
lines: [calm] I'm asking you to explain it.

scenes.image: Ryan snatching the papers off the counter.
lines: He grabbed the papers. But not before Emma had seen enough. [pause] And not before she quietly took a photo of the first page.
scenes.motion: he sweeps the stack of papers off the counter and turns away

scenes.image: Emma at the counter, worried; Ryan at the door with his coat half on.
lines: [softer, worried] Ryan... are we in trouble?
[quiet] Then look me in the eye.

scenes.image: Ryan at the door turning back, his face cold.
lines: [cold, deliberate] My mother was right about you.

scenes.image: Ryan sitting alone in his parked car in an office garage, phone to his ear, rubbing his forehead.
sfx: Phone ringing, then a car interior

scenes.image: Victoria in her study, phone pressed to her ear, standing at the window, her reflection in the glass.
lines: [icy] Then stop giving her opportunities to ask.

scenes.image: Close-up of Victoria, a slow calculating smile.
lines: [patient, like explaining to a child] No, darling. You need her cooperation. There's a difference.
And how am I supposed to get it?
[softly] Make her understand what she stands to lose.

scenes.image: Victoria turning from the window, decision made.
lines: Thanksgiving is in three weeks. Bring her. [pause] I'll handle the rest.

scenes.image: Ryan in his car, hesitating, phone at his ear.
lines: [hard] Do you want to save your company or not?

scenes.image: Ryan staring at his phone screen in the dark car, the glow on his face.
lines: Ryan stared at his phone. Then he opened an email from the lender.

scenes.image: Grace walking down the dim upstairs hallway, stopping at a door left ajar with voices inside.
sfx: Footsteps on hardwood in a quiet hallway

scenes.image: Grace freezing in the hallway, listening at the gap of the door.
lines: [muffled, through the door] She has to believe she's losing everything, Ryan.
[muffled] Then we move to the second option.
scenes.motion: she stops mid-step and slowly leans toward the half-open door

scenes.image: Close-up of Grace's face, eyes widening, holding her breath.
lines: [muffled, anxious] You promised we wouldn't need that.

scenes.image: Grace pushing the study door open; Victoria and Ryan turning, startled.
lines: [startled, then composed] Grace! How long have you been standing there?

scenes.image: Ryan waving it off; Grace crossing her arms, unconvinced.
lines: [sarcastic] Since when is Emma part of your business negotiations?

scenes.image: Grace backing out of the doorway, eyes on her mother.
lines: [pointed] So is whatever you're planning for Thanksgiving.

scenes.image: Grace walking away down the hallway, jaw set, glancing back once.
lines: Grace walked away. [pause] But she didn't believe a word of it.

scenes.image: Thanksgiving afternoon: Emma carrying two homemade pies into the mansion's marble kitchen.
lines: Thanksgiving. Emma had been in Victoria's kitchen since seven a.m.
[cheerful, trying] Victoria, where do you want the pies?
sfx: Busy kitchen, oven timer beeping, pots clanking

scenes.image: Victoria not even looking up from arranging flowers; Emma holding a pecan pie.
Emma setting the pie down, studying Victoria.
lines: [too sweet] Why would something be wrong?
You've barely spoken to me all morning.

scenes.image: Victoria walking out of the kitchen with the flower vase, not looking back.
lines: [clipped] I'm hosting fourteen people, Emma. I have responsibilities. [pause] Perhaps you should finish setting the table.
scenes.motion: she sweeps out of the kitchen carrying the vase without looking back

scenes.image: Emma setting the long dining table alone, laying silverware, the chandelier above.
lines: So Emma set the table. Fourteen places. And on the sideboard, under a stack of holiday cards, she noticed an envelope.
sfx: Silverware being placed on a table, quiet room

scenes.image: Close-up of an official-looking envelope on a sideboard, a return-address logo with a small oak tree emblem, the printed text soft and unreadable.
lines: [slowly] The return address said Ashford Family Trust. [pause] Ashford. Her grandmother's name.

scenes.image: Emma holding the envelope, puzzled, glancing toward the doorway.
lines: Before she could think about it, footsteps.
[low, urgent] Emma. Can I talk to you?

scenes.image: Grace pulling Emma into a corner of the dining room, speaking quietly.
lines: [whispering] Did Ryan ask you to sign anything recently?
Some business papers. I said no.

scenes.image: Close-up of Grace, relieved and worried at once.
Grace glancing toward the hallway as someone calls her name, gripping Emma's arm.
lines: [urgent whisper] Emma... whatever happens tonight, don't sign anything.

scenes.image: Thanksgiving dinner in full swing: fourteen guests around the long candlelit table, the chandelier glowing, a carved turkey.
lines: Seven fifteen. Fourteen guests. Candles lit. The turkey carved. [pause] And then Victoria stood up.
sfx: Dinner guests laughing and chatting, glasses clinking

scenes.image: Victoria standing at the head of the table, raising her champagne glass with a gracious smile.
lines: [gracious, smiling] I'd like to make a toast.
[the smile freezing] To knowing who deserves to be called family.

scenes.image: Victoria setting her glass down hard, her face turning cold.
sfx: Glass set down hard on a table

scenes.image: Emma slowly standing, confused, while guests exchange looks.
lines: Victoria, if there's a problem, we can talk after dinner.
[loud] Oh, no. I want everyone to hear this.

scenes.image: Victoria addressing the guests like a speech, gesturing at Emma.
lines: [theatrical] For four years, I have tolerated a woman who married my son for his money. She came into this family with nothing. No money. No connections. [pause] Not even a respectable family name.

scenes.image: Close-up of Emma, cheeks burning, voice shaking but firm.
lines: [shaking] That's not true. [firmer] And don't talk about my family.
[contempt] Then stop pretending you're one of us.

scenes.image: Emma turning to Ryan beside her; Ryan staring at his plate.
lines: [mumbling] Emma, please. Don't make this worse.

scenes.image: Victoria checking a delicate gold watch on her wrist, smiling.
lines: [cold, savoring it] You have ten minutes to collect your things and get out of my house.
sfx: Guests gasping, a fork dropping on a plate

scenes.image: Emma staring at Victoria in disbelief.
lines: [disbelief] You're throwing me out... on Thanksgiving?
[sweetly] Consider it my holiday gift to you.

scenes.image: Ryan finally looking up, weak and guilty.
lines: [can't look at her] Maybe it's better if you go. Just for tonight. We'll talk tomorrow.

scenes.image: Emma pushing her chair back, standing tall, eyes wet but steady.
lines: [quiet, breaking] Four years. [pause] Four years, and you can't even stand up for me.
sfx: A chair scraping back on a wooden floor

scenes.image: Close-up of Emma's hand sliding off her wedding ring and setting it beside her untouched plate.
lines: Emma slowly took off her wedding ring. And set it down beside her untouched plate.
scenes.motion: she slides the ring off her finger and places it gently on the tablecloth

scenes.image: Emma looking straight at Victoria across the table.
lines: [steady] Before I go, Victoria. One question.
[slow, deliberate] Are you absolutely certain this house belongs to you?

scenes.image: Close-up of Victoria, a flicker of fear behind the scoff.
lines: [scoffs, too quickly] Of course it does.
[calm] Then I hope you have the paperwork.
sfx: Music cuts out, a deep cinematic boom

scenes.image: Emma in her coat walking out through the mansion's grand front doors into the cold dark rain.
lines: [calling after her] Your ten minutes are almost up!
[not turning around] Keep your ten minutes.
sfx: Heavy front door slamming, rain outside
scenes.motion: she walks out the front doors into the rain without looking back

scenes.image: Emma in her car at a gas station in pouring rain, mascara running, gripping the steering wheel.
lines: Emma made it as far as a gas station two miles away. Then she couldn't drive anymore.
[crying, to herself] Come on, Ryan. Call me. Tell me you're sorry.
sfx: Heavy rain on a car roof, engine idling

scenes.image: Emma grabbing her buzzing phone off the passenger seat.
lines: [calm, gravelly] Emma? It's Martin Brooks. Your grandmother's attorney.

scenes.image: Mr. Brooks at his desk late at night, lamp on, phone to his ear, a thick file open.
lines: [apologetic] I'm sorry to call on Thanksgiving. But we have a serious problem. The property at 18 Ashford Lane.

scenes.image: Close-up of Mr. Brooks, grave.
lines: [measured] Emma... that house belongs to your grandmother's family trust. It has for twelve years.

scenes.image: Emma frozen in the car, rain streaming down the windshield, her face lit by neon.
lines: Victoria has an occupancy agreement. She lives there. She doesn't own it.
scenes.motion: rain streams down the windshield as she sits completely still

scenes.image: Emma pressing her hand against her forehead.
lines: [slowly] And you're telling me this tonight because...?
[grave] Because someone tried to use that house as collateral for a three-million-dollar loan.

scenes.image: Close-up of Emma's eyes hardening.
lines: [careful] Come to my office in the morning. First, we protect the trust. Then we find out exactly who signed what.

scenes.image: Next morning: Mr. Brooks opening a thick folder across his desk to Emma.
lines: Your grandmother bought that house fifteen years ago. After Victoria's family lost almost everything.
sfx: Quiet office, folder opening, papers rustling

scenes.image: Emma shaking her head, overwhelmed.
lines: Why didn't she ever tell me?
[gentle] She wanted you to build your own life. Without the weight of other people's expectations.

scenes.image: Close-up of an appraisal document and a photo of the Connecticut mansion clipped to it, the printed text soft and unreadable.
lines: How much is the house worth?
The last appraisal? About six million dollars. [pause] And it's one of eleven properties in the trust.

scenes.image: Emma sitting back, stunned, almost laughing.
lines: [a stunned laugh] Eleven. [pause] Victoria spent four years calling me poor.
[dry] She knew she didn't own that house.

scenes.image: Mr. Brooks shaking his head slowly.
lines: I don't believe she knew you were the primary beneficiary.
[slowly] So the woman who threw me out of her mansion...
[evenly] Was living in a house that belongs to your grandmother's trust.
sfx: Long tense silence, a clock ticking

scenes.image: Close-up of Emma, the hurt in her eyes turning to resolve.
lines: [firm] Mr. Brooks? [pause] I want to see the loan documents.

scenes.image: Close-up of loan documents slid across the desk, two signature lines visible, the printed text soft and unreadable.
lines: That's Ryan's company. Parker Holdings. And that's his signature.
sfx: Paper sliding across a wooden desk

scenes.image: Emma pointing at the second signature; Brooks leaning back.
lines: And who signed here? The trustee line.
[flat] I've never seen this document in my life.

scenes.image: Emma pulling out her phone, scrolling to a photo.
lines: [quickly] Three weeks ago Ryan tried to make me sign something. I said no. [pause] But I took a picture.

scenes.image: Mr. Brooks zooming in on Emma's phone, eyebrows rising.
lines: [slowly] Interesting. These name a second borrower. Another two million dollars.

scenes.image: Emma staring out the rainy window, betrayed.
lines: [hollow] Ryan told me everything was fine.
[grim] Then your husband has a great deal of explaining to do.

scenes.image: Emma outside the law office building in the rain, answering her phone.
lines: [dry] Somewhere you can't throw me out.
sfx: Rain on a sidewalk, a phone ringing

scenes.image: Ryan pacing in the mansion study with his phone.
lines: [sarcastic] Very funny. Listen, we need to talk about the documents.
sfx: A beat of silence on a phone line

scenes.image: Ryan stopping dead, his face draining.
lines: The three-million-dollar loan? [pause] Or the other two million?

scenes.image: Emma under an awning in the rain, phone at her ear, cold and composed.
lines: [controlled anger] Emma, listen carefully. Those are confidential business matters.
You tried to make me sign them.

scenes.image: Ryan shouting into the phone, red-faced.
Emma with the phone, eyes steady, rain behind her.
lines: [threatening, low] If you do that, I'll make sure you walk away with nothing.
[almost amused] You already tried that on Thanksgiving.

scenes.image: Ryan gripping the phone, sneering.
lines: [steady] No, Ryan. [pause] I think I'm finally paying attention.

scenes.image: Ryan bursting into the study and shutting the door; Victoria looking up from her desk.
lines: [panicked] Mom. Emma knows about the loans.

scenes.image: Victoria rising from her desk, eyes narrowing.
lines: [bitter] That man has always been a problem.
We need another way to get the money.
[slowly] You told me the paperwork was valid.

scenes.image: Ryan unable to meet his mother's eyes.
lines: [evasive] It was supposed to be. Someone questioned the trustee authorization.
[quietly, dangerous] Ryan. Did you forge that signature?

scenes.image: Close-up of Ryan, sweating, choosing his words.
lines: [evasive] I had Trent prepare the documents.
[weak] I didn't personally sign his name.

scenes.image: Victoria sinking into her chair, a hand over her mouth.
lines: [shaking] How much trouble are we in?

scenes.image: Ryan leaning on the desk, defeated.
lines: [hollow] More than you know. [pause] The company could collapse before Christmas.

scenes.image: Late at night: Grace confronting Victoria by the fireplace in the formal living room.
lines: [direct] Mom. Why did you tell everyone you owned this house?
sfx: Crackling fireplace in a large quiet room

scenes.image: Victoria staring into the fire, her composure cracking.
lines: [quietly] Your father lost almost everything. Fifteen years ago. We were weeks from losing the house.
scenes.motion: firelight flickers across her face as she stares into the flames

scenes.image: Grace stunned, sitting down slowly on the arm of a chair.
Close-up of Victoria, ashamed, twisting her pearls.
lines: She had her trust buy the house. And she let us stay. [pause] For twelve years.

scenes.image: Grace standing up, furious.
lines: [angry] Because you spent four years treating her like she was beneath us!
[weak] I didn't know she was the beneficiary.

scenes.image: Grace at the doorway, turning back to her mother by the fire.
lines: [quiet] You know what the worst part is? [pause] Emma would've helped you. Even if she'd never known about the house.

scenes.image: Emma at a coffee shop window table, looking up in surprise as someone sits down.
lines: [awkward, sincere] I owe you an apology.
sfx: Quiet coffee shop, rain outside, cups clinking

scenes.image: Grace with both hands around a coffee cup, eyes down, ashamed.
lines: [quiet] For laughing when Mom insulted you. For not saying anything. For pretending it was normal.

scenes.image: Emma softening, touched.
lines: [leaning in] There's something else. Ryan knew Mom was going to throw you out.

scenes.image: Grace leaning across the table, serious.
lines: No. I mean they planned it. Weeks before Thanksgiving. [pause] Ryan needed you scared enough to sign.
[slowly] So the whole dinner was staged?

scenes.image: The two women facing each other across the small table.
lines: I heard Mom say you had to believe you were losing everything.
sfx: A coffee cup set down on a saucer

scenes.image: Close-up of Emma, calm resolve settling over her face.
lines: What are you going to do?
[quiet, final] I'm going to stop protecting him.

scenes.image: Victoria opening the mansion's front door to find Emma standing there in her coat.
lines: Four days after Thanksgiving, the doorbell rang at 18 Ashford Lane.
[startled] Emma? What are you doing here?
sfx: Doorbell chime echoing in a large house

scenes.image: Mr. Brooks stepping into the foyer with a briefcase; Ryan coming down the staircase, freezing.
lines: We need to discuss this property. And some disputed financing documents.

scenes.image: Victoria drawing herself up, outraged.
lines: [evenly] Your home, yes. [pause] Your property? No.

scenes.image: Mr. Brooks laying a copy of a deed on the coffee table.
lines: [calm] The Ashford Family Trust holds the deed.
[shrill] I've lived here for twelve years!

scenes.image: Ryan stepping toward Emma, angry; Emma unmoved.
lines: [cold] What's ridiculous is trying to borrow five million dollars using documents you wouldn't let me read.

scenes.image: Emma turning to face the whole room, arms crossed.
sfx: Heavy silence in a large room

scenes.image: Ryan with his mouth open, nothing coming out; Emma waiting.
lines: [quiet, pointed] Go ahead, Ryan. [pause] We're listening.

scenes.image: Victoria turning to her son, her voice shaking.
Ryan cornered by the fireplace, hands raised.
lines: [sharp] With Mr. Brooks's signature on it?

scenes.image: Mr. Brooks calmly checking his phone, then looking up.
lines: [dry] Interesting you'd say that. Trent called the lender this morning. [pause] He told them you asked him to sign my name.

scenes.image: Close-up of Ryan's face collapsing, color draining.
Grace stepping forward from the doorway.
lines: [cold] Ryan, you told me Emma was stealing money from the company.

scenes.image: Emma turning slowly to Ryan, hurt and furious.
lines: [slow fury] I worked for you for almost a year without a real salary.
[steel] That didn't make my work free.

scenes.image: Victoria gripping the back of a chair, looking at her son like a stranger.
lines: [quietly] Ryan... how much of this is true?
[desperate] I was trying to save the business!

scenes.image: Close-up of Emma, calm and devastating.
lines: [quiet] You had plenty of choices, Ryan. [pause] You just kept choosing the ones that hurt other people.

scenes.image: Victoria sitting down slowly on the sofa, suddenly old and small.
lines: For the first time in four years, Victoria Parker had nothing to say. [pause] Almost nothing.

scenes.image: Victoria looking up at Emma standing before her.
Emma looking down at Victoria, hurt in her eyes.
lines: I didn't know about the trust.
[quiet] You knew Grandma saved your family.
And you still called my family worthless.

scenes.image: Close-up of Victoria, tears in her eyes, finally honest.
lines: [softly] That's the first honest thing you've said to me in four years.

scenes.image: Victoria clutching her pearls, frightened.
Emma standing straight, composed and fair.
lines: [even] The trustees will decide. [pause] I'm not going to throw you into the street, Victoria. But I'm not going to protect you from what you did, either.

scenes.image: Victoria reaching out a trembling hand; Emma not taking it.
lines: [quiet] Funny. That's what I said on Thanksgiving. [pause] And nobody listened.

scenes.image: Ryan stepping toward Emma, desperate, reaching for her hands.
lines: [desperate, soft] Emma, please. We can fix this. Our marriage.

scenes.image: Emma pulling her hands away, calm.
lines: [calm] You loved having someone who'd do anything for you.
[steel] Neither was what you did to me.

scenes.image: Ryan spreading his hands, broken.
lines: A divorce. [pause] And a full accounting of every dollar that went through your company.

scenes.image: Ryan turning red; Mr. Brooks stepping forward with a folder.
lines: [calm] She doesn't have to. The lender's fraud unit already has. And so does the state's attorney.

scenes.image: Close-up of divorce papers set down on the coffee table next to the deed.
lines: Emma placed a single envelope on the table. Divorce papers. Already signed. [pause] Her signature. The only one in this story that was real.
sfx: An envelope set down on a table

scenes.image: Ryan staring at the papers, shaking.
lines: [calm] No, Ryan. You made those decisions. [pause] I'm just refusing to pay for them.

scenes.image: Emma buttoning her coat at the front door, looking back once.
lines: [quiet] You told me to leave on Thanksgiving. Remember?
[final] This time, I'm leaving because I choose to.
sfx: Footsteps on marble, a heavy door closing
scenes.motion: she turns and walks out through the front door, closing it behind her

scenes.image: Wide shot: Ryan staring at the papers, Victoria on the sofa, Grace looking at the empty doorway, the fire dying.
lines: [slow] Ryan stared at the papers. Victoria stared at the deed. And Grace looked at the empty doorway. [pause] For the first time, the Parker family had run out of people to blame.

scenes.image: One year later: Emma and Grace laughing in a cozy small kitchen, a homemade turkey and pies on the counter.
sfx: Warm kitchen sounds, soft acoustic Thanksgiving music, friends chatting

scenes.image: Grace pointing at a pecan pie, grinning.
lines: [teasing] You made the pecan pie? [laughs] Mom used to complain about your pies.

scenes.image: Wide shot of the small dining table with a few friends, candles and homemade food, autumn leaves outside.
lines: One year after the worst Thanksgiving of her life, Emma was hosting dinner in her grandmother's little house. No chandeliers. No marble. Just people who were glad she was there.
scenes.motion: candles flicker as friends pass dishes around the small table

scenes.image: Ryan in a cheap suit leaving a courthouse alone, head down, gray winter day.
lines: Ryan pleaded guilty to bank fraud. Trent's testimony saw to that. His company is gone. He'll spend the next three years in federal prison.
sfx: Courthouse steps, cold wind, a car door

scenes.image: Victoria alone in a small plain rented apartment, unpacking boxes, no chandelier, no guests.
lines: Victoria moved out of 18 Ashford Lane in January. She rents a two-bedroom condo now. [pause] Not one of her fourteen Thanksgiving guests has called.

scenes.image: Emma opening the door to Mr. Brooks holding a small wooden box.
lines: And Emma went back to work as an interior designer.
[warm] That must be Mr. Brooks. Come in!
[gentle] Happy Thanksgiving, Emma. I brought something your grandmother wanted you to have.
sfx: Doorbell, a door opening, cold wind

scenes.image: Close-up of an old cassette recorder in a wooden box on the table, a hand pressing play.
